name: Tianyi
description: A star 246 parsecs away, 72 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 62423: radius 72.281 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1017.44 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.175) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 62423: effective temperature 3837 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.106)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 62423: distance 246.17 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.163), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 246 parsecs away, 72 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,017 times the Sun's luminosity at 3,837 K, so 72.281 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 62423: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: 7 Draconis
quotes.card: 7 Draconis, also named Tianyi, is a single star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Draco.
quotes.introduction: It is visible to the naked eye as a faint orange-hued star with a stellar classification of 5.43.
